internal.title: SEV1: Checkout Service Errors Due to Payment Service Failure
internal.body:
At 11:24 UTC, we received alerts for a high error rate in the checkout service. Diagnosis identified a 100% error rate and elevated latency in the payment service as the root cause, which was confirmed by a 95% error rate and high latency in checkout. The issue was resolved by disabling the paymentFailure flag at 11:44 UTC, after which error rates returned to normal. The incident lasted approximately 20 minutes.

Timeline:
- 11:24:21 Alert received for checkout service error rate spike
- 11:44:07 Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 11:44:15 PaymentFailure flag disabled
- 11:44:15 Recovery verified with normalized error rates

Actions taken:
- Disabled paymentFailure flag to stop error injection

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment service issues
external.body: Between 11:24 and 11:44 UTC, some customers experienced failures when attempting to complete checkout due to issues in the payment processing service. The problem was identified and resolved within 20 minutes, and normal service has been restored. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

output.summary: A high error rate in the checkout service was caused by a failure in the payment service, which was resolved by disabling a problematic feature flag.
output.impact: Customers experienced failures completing checkout for approximately 20 minutes due to payment service errors.
output.root_cause: The payment service experienced a 100% error rate and elevated latency due to an error injection triggered by the paymentFailure flag.
output.resolution: The paymentFailure flag was disabled, stopping the error injection and restoring normal service operation.

lessons.lesson: Feature flags that trigger error injections should have additional safeguards and monitoring to prevent widespread service impact.
lessons.applies_when: When a feature flag causes a high error rate in the payment service due to error injection.

lessons.lesson: High error rates in downstream services (like payment) can propagate and severely impact upstream services (like checkout), so cross-service monitoring is critical.
lessons.applies_when: When errors in a downstream service cause high error rates in an upstream service.

action_items: Implement additional safeguards and monitoring on feature flags that trigger error injections.
Enhance cross-service alerting to detect and correlate error spikes between dependent services.
